Thanks Mina. Quick technical note in case it's useful for records: when an Outlook client forwards a gCal invite that contains an embedded Meet, some clients serialize the event as plain text and strip the <a href> anchor — that leaves the event body with a visible label but no clickable URL. The underlying Meet token can still be present in the raw iCal, but many enterprise mail gateways sanitize HTML.

Options (pros/cons):
- Recreate event on Redwood Zoom and send new invite: simplest, guaranteed clickable URL for Outlook recipients.
- Resend original gCal but instruct recipients to "Add to calendar" rather than use forwarded message: lower effort but fragile (depends on recipients' clients).
- Provision a temporary co-host service account for Redwood on your Zoom (we create meeting as 'Redwood Demo - Apex Health') so organizer metadata is clear for audit. Requires a quick allowlist for the service account (I can drop instructions).

If you want the temp host flow, I can:
1) Create the Zoom meeting and generate a plain-text join link.
2) Send a fresh .ics and gCal invite to the distribution list.
3) Confirm host/co-host settings and disable recording if Apex requests that.

Mina — if you give me the green light I'll spin this up and send the new invite (I can do it in the next 20 minutes).

— Ben
Product Operations Engineer | Redwood Inference
